title: Malleable software: Restoring user agency
context: Ink & Switch — software should adapt to users, not the other way around. Users shouldn't be forced into someone else's workflow.

title: Capture the Why
context: The gap between saving content and understanding why you saved it. Every bookmark is an unanswered question about yourself.

title: Users as routers between software silos
context: 'We became users. We had to adapt our thinking and actions to the software.' The human is the only integration layer between apps.

title: End-User Programming
context: Ink & Switch — vision of users as creators, not consumers of software. What if everyone could modify the tools they use?

title: Dynamicland — Bret Victor
context: Computing that lives in the physical world. Radical rethinking of what an interface is. No screens, no apps — just shared physical space.

title: What if the tool could see across all my apps?
context: Frustration with context fragmentation — each app is a silo, the user is the only integration layer. I want ONE thing that sees everything.

title: Local-first software: You own your data
context: Ink & Switch — CRDTs, offline-first, data ownership. Your data should live on your device, sync when convenient, never held hostage by a server.

title: automerge
context: CRDT library for building local-first collaborative applications. Conflict-free merging without a central server.

title: Computers and Creativity — Molly Mielke
context: How computational tools can augment human creativity rather than replace it. The best tools amplify, not automate.

title: The problem isn't information overload. The problem is that no tool helps you see the SHAPE of what you care about.
